assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based and skill-biased account of technology and trade, plus the measured labour-market effects of import competition, changed how economists and policymakers understand wage inequality and labour demand. It has strong empirical and conceptual reach, and it connects to the capital-skill complementarity literature. The case is among the most compelling on this list.
assessment.attribution: Katz is the long-run anchor through the supply-demand-and-technology framework and the returns-to-skill evidence. Autor is central to the task approach and the labour-market polarization evidence. Hanson is central to the trade-shock evidence, with Dorn a close co-author. Three names capture the core, but Dorn is left out, and the task framework also draws on work by others, including laureates from 2023 and 2024.
assessment.maturity: Foundational work dates from the early 1990s and early 2000s, and the trade-shock literature has been replicated and debated for more than a decade. The evidence is mature enough to act on.
uncertainties: Overlap with the topics of the 2023 and 2024 prizes, which affects how the committee would frame the citation.
Whether the trade-shock work and the technology-task work should be cited together or separately.
Ongoing debate over the persistence and size of the China-shock effects.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral constraints and the amplification of shocks through credit are a core mechanism in modern macroeconomics. The 2008 crisis and its aftermath made the framework central to the field. It is a clean theoretical contribution with a very large downstream literature and policy use.
assessment.attribution: The 1997 Kiyotaki-Moore paper is the clear originating contribution, so two laureates are sufficient. Gertler and Gilchrist are important for the financial accelerator and its empirical side, but including them would blur the citation. Bernanke's earlier prize covered related ground.
assessment.maturity: The work is almost thirty years old, widely taught and embedded in DSGE and quantitative models. Its relevance has been confirmed by the crisis experience.
uncertainties: Partial overlap with the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises.
Whether the committee prefers to pair this with the financial accelerator or with the broader New Keynesian prize.
Direct empirical tests of the mechanism remain mixed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Staggered pricing, nominal rigidities and the New Keynesian framework are the workhorse of monetary policy analysis in central banks worldwide. This is one of the most consequential macroeconomic advances of the past four decades.
assessment.attribution: This is the hardest list to cap at three. Calvo and Taylor supplied the price-setting building blocks and Woodford the integrated policy framework. Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets, among others, are also major contributors, especially on empirical DSGE estimation. Any three-name selection will be contested.
assessment.maturity: The work spans 1980 to the 2000s, has long been validated in practice and has been tested through several policy regimes.
uncertainties: Attribution among at least eight credited names, with a likely alternative triple such as Gali, Gertler and Woodford.
Whether post-2008 and post-2021 inflation experience weakens the empirical standing of the framework.
The committee may prefer a narrower citation, for example price-setting or the policy rule.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity transformed international trade theory and empirics. It explains who exports, how gains from trade operate through selection and reallocation, and why aggregate outcomes depend on micro structure. It has had very wide influence in quantitative trade work and in macroeconomics.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the pivotal model, and Helpman's earlier work and his heterogeneous-firm papers with Melitz and Yeaple connect the framework to evidence. Redding is important for quantitative extensions but is a later contributor. Krugman's 2008 prize covered the earlier new trade theory, and others such as Bernard, Eaton and Kortum are outside this credited list.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of use, testing and extension. This is a settled and widely taught result.
uncertainties: Contributions by researchers not credited here, such as Bernard, Jensen, Eaton, Kortum and Yeaple, complicate attribution.
Whether Helpman's broader body of work should be cited instead or as well.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Measuring misallocation of resources across firms gave a disciplined way to link micro distortions to aggregate productivity and cross-country income gaps. It has reshaped quantitative growth and development economics and policy diagnostics. The conceptual and measurement contribution is substantial, but measurement challenges temper it.
assessment.attribution: The 2009 Hsieh-Klenow paper is the central and most cited contribution. Restuccia and Rogerson's closely related work is also important, and Restuccia is credited here, so the choice of two versus three names is debatable.
assessment.maturity: The approach has been used for over fifteen years and is widely replicated, though the interpretation of measured wedges is still debated.
uncertainties: The interpretation of measured misallocation is sensitive to measurement error, markups and adjustment costs.
Whether Restuccia should be added, and how to treat Rogerson, who is not credited here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Weak instruments and identification-robust inference changed everyday applied practice, because first-stage strength and robust confidence sets are now standard. This is a methodological contribution with very broad empirical impact, and it follows the 2021 prize that recognised instrumental variables for causal analysis.
assessment.attribution: Staiger and Stock (1997) established the practical importance of weak instruments. Andrews contributed foundational general theory of robust inference. Moreira, Yogo and others developed the conditional and robust tests, and Stock is also credited in other lists. Credit is distributed across theory and application.
assessment.maturity: About thirty years of development with standard-practice status, so maturity is high.
uncertainties: Diffuse attribution among five credited names and others.
Econometrics prizes are rare and the committee may prioritise a different methods topic.
Distinguishing Andrews's broader econometric theory work from the weak-instrument contributions specifically.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Persson and Tabellini built a systematic political economics that connects electoral rules, constitutions and fiscal outcomes with both theory and empirical testing. The agenda is a major research area. It is broad and influential, though the 2024 prize already recognised institutions and growth.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the clear core pair through their joint books and papers. Besley is an important independent contributor, especially on state capacity, and could be added. I disclose a possible proximity conflict: Persson is, to my knowledge, at the IIES. That is not in the supplied profile, and I do not adjudicate it. My own work on the political economy of growth is also in an adjacent area.
assessment.maturity: The agenda spans thirty years and has been extensively tested, with identification challenges in the observational evidence.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 prize and with the broader institutions agenda.
Whether Besley should be included and how the committee would compare state-capacity work with the electoral-rules work.
Possible conflict, disclosed and not adjudicated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Methods for estimating demand and supply in differentiated-product markets, together with dynamic industry models, underpin modern empirical industrial organisation, merger analysis and antitrust. This is a widely used tool-building contribution with real policy application.
assessment.attribution: The BLP framework (Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes) is the core and Pakes is also central to dynamic models such as Ericson-Pakes. Bresnahan, Benkard, Levin and Reiss contributed related methods, so a three-name cap leaves out important contributors.
assessment.maturity: The framework dates from the mid-1990s and is standard practice, so maturity is high.
uncertainties: Attribution across seven credited names, with a large field of related work.
Whether the committee would treat this as a narrower methods prize relative to the broader macro and labour candidates ranked above.
